query: How can we reduce declined expense submissions?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing expenses by asset type gives a genuine grouping axis to compare decline rates across purchase types. Values are mostly sound readings of short_description/ci, though 'Provision of Services for iPod touch' -> software_service is a debatable but defensible read.

per_column.name: submission_context_pattern
per_column.rationale: How a submission originated (auto-generated vs manual vs acquisition) is highly relevant to declines. However the source text shows no clear signal distinguishing 'manually_submitted' from 'acquisition_purchase'; e.g. 'Asset assignment for new Dell Laptop' -> acquisition vs 'Provision of Services' -> manual appears inferred beyond what the text supports.

per_column.name: department_group
per_column.rationale: A department axis would help, but an original 'department' column already exists making this largely redundant. More critically, the source samples provided contain no department evidence, yet specific departments (sales, product_management, customer_support) are confidently assigned to asset-description text, suggesting invented or unwarranted values.

per_column.name: submission_completeness_signal
per_column.rationale: Completeness of a submission is plausibly linked to declines, giving analytical leverage. But it is a near-binary flag whose basis is unclear from the source text; rows with 'nan' processed_date and terse descriptions are still marked True, so the value is not clearly derivable.

per_column.name: travel_expense_indicator
per_column.rationale: Isolating travel expenses is a reasonable comparison axis for declines, though it is a bare binary flag with limited leverage. The samples shown are all non-travel and correctly marked False, so groundedness appears sound on available evidence.

per_column.name: description_specificity_level
per_column.rationale: Vague/templated descriptions plausibly correlate with declines, offering a useful axis. Values track the text well: 'Dell OptiPlex 7050' -> specific_model_or_brand, 'Miscellaneous hardware component' -> generic_category are sound readings.

judge.rationale: Most columns offer genuine grouping/modeling axes relevant to reducing declines (asset type, submission context, description specificity, travel flag). Groundedness is the weaker dimension: department_group duplicates an existing column and, along with submission_context_pattern and submission_completeness_signal, assigns confident specifics not clearly supported by the sampled source text. Columns grounded in the description/ci text (asset_category_type, description_specificity_level, travel_expense_indicator) are the strongest.
